content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS BUT NO ONE HANDS YOU AT THE {{HOSPITAL}}
facts: **Hydrate before you eat** – chug a glass of water the moment you wake up, breastfeeding and sleep deprivation both drain fluids fast.
**Eat standing at the counter** – don't wait for a 'proper' sit-down meal, 5 minutes of real food beats skipping it for 2 hours.
**Keep protein bars by the crib** – one handful of nuts or a bar at 3am keeps blood sugar steady so you don't crash by sunrise.
**Nap when the baby naps, once a day minimum** – even 20 minutes lowers cortisol enough to make the next stretch manageable.
**Batch-cook on day one** – freeze single portions of soup or rice so week two doesn't become takeout every night.
**Step outside for 10 minutes daily** – sunlight resets your circadian rhythm even if your sleep schedule is completely broken.
**Ask for one specific task, not 'help'** – say 'bring dinner Tuesday' instead of 'let me know if you need anything,' it actually gets done.
**Track your own meals, not just the baby's** – a sticky note of what and when you ate prevents accidental 10-hour fasting.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
New parents, a few of these matter more than they sound. Protein bars by the crib work because overnight feeds spike your hunger hormones right when you're least likely to cook anything — having something within arm's reach stops the blood sugar crash that makes you feel shaky and irritable the next morning. Batch-cooking on day one matters because decision fatigue hits hardest in week two, once the adrenaline of birth wears off and exhaustion catches up — having frozen meals removes one decision entirely on your worst days. And stepping outside for 10 minutes daily isn't just 'fresh air' advice — morning light exposure helps re-anchor your circadian rhythm even when your actual sleep hours are chaotic, which makes falling back asleep between feeds easier. Everyone's recovery looks different, listen to your own body.
